methods.name: to_dict
methods.summary: Return the config as the JSON-ready dict `adapter_config.json` holds.
methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.  A field the reference's config of this method lacks
(`IA3Config.layers_to_transform`) is written only when it is set,
so a file that does not use it is one the reference reads too.

returns.description: One entry per field, keyed by the reference's field names.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> d = LoraConfig(target_modules=["v", "q"], task_type="CAUSAL_LM").to_dict()
>>> d["target_modules"], d["task_type"], d["peft_type"]
(['q', 'v'], 'CAUSAL_LM', 'LORA')

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"loftq_config": {}`, `"megatron_config": null`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is dropped.  Called on
`PeftConfig`, the dict's `peft_type` picks the class.

parameters.name: config_dict
parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class the dict's method names.

raises.description:
The dict describes another adapter type, or turns on a feature
v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.summary: Write `adapter_config.json` into `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
The file is the reference's: `to_dict` with its keys sorted,
indented by two spaces.  The directory is created if missing.

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
`auto_mapping_dict` replaces the `auto_mapping` the file records.
The reference forwards any other keyword to its hub upload; there
is no hub here, so another key raises.

raises.description: `save_directory` names an existing file.
`kwargs` holds a key other than `auto_mapping_dict`.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d).r
2

methods.name: from_json_file
methods.summary: Read a config file into the dict it holds, unchanged but for `runtime_config`.
methods.extended:
What `from_pretrained` reads before it chooses a config class: the
file's content as a dict, as the reference's `from_json_file` returns
it.  `from_dict` turns it into a config.

parameters.name: path_json_file
parameters.description: The path of a JSON file such as `adapter_config.json`.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
Accepted for the reference's signature; it passes none to the
reader, and any key given here raises.

returns.description:
The file's object, without a `runtime_config` key: the
reference warns that such a key is ignored, since a runtime
configuration is valid at runtime only.

raises.description: There is no file at `path_json_file`.
The file does not hold a JSON object.
`kwargs` is not empty.

examples:
>>> import os, tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     raw = PeftConfig.from_json_file(os.path.join(d, "adapter_config.json"))
>>> raw["peft_type"], raw["r"]
('LORA', 2)

methods.signature: from_pretrained(pretrained_model_name_or_path: str | os.PathLike[str], subfolder: str | None = None, kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Read `adapter_config.json` from a local adapter directory.
methods.extended:
The file's `peft_type` picks the config class: called on

The reference forwards these to its hub download (`revision`,

...     loaded = LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d)
>>> loaded.r, loaded.lora_alpha, loaded.target_modules

members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with VeRA.
members.extended:
VeRA (Kopiczko et al., 2023, [arXiv:2310.11454](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11454) — Vector-based Random Matrix
Adaptation) freezes the model **and** the low-rank pair: one random matrix
$A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{in}}$ and one
$B \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times r}$ are drawn once and shared by every
targeted layer (sliced to its size), and a layer learns only two vectors,

$$
\qquad \lambda_d \in \mathbb{R}^{r},\; \lambda_b \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}.
$$

$\lambda_b$ starts at zero, so the adapted model starts as the base.
The update folds into the weight exactly, so a merged model costs what the
base does.

Field names, their order, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference
adapter library's.  Unlike the reference's,
this config also takes `exclude_modules`, which selects modules the way
`LoraConfig`'s does.

parameters.name: task_type
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.name: peft_type
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.name: auto_mapping
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.name: peft_version
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.name: base_model_name_or_path
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.name: inference_mode
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.name: r
parameters.description:
The shared projections' rank.  VeRA trains far fewer parameters than LoRA
at a given rank, so it takes ranks far above LoRA's.

parameters.name: target_modules
parameters.description:
The `nn.Linear` modules to adapt, matched as `LoraConfig.target_modules`
is.  `None` takes the default for the base model's `model_type`
(`VERA_DEFAULT_TARGET_MODULES` in `lucid.peft.tuners.vera._defaults`);
another model type raises `ValueError`.

parameters.name: projection_prng_key
parameters.description:
Seed of the generator the shared `vera_A` / `vera_B` are drawn from
(Kaiming-uniform, as the reference does).  The same key gives the same
projections on every device, so an adapter saved without them
(`save_projection=False`) reloads exactly.

parameters.name: save_projection
parameters.description:
Write `vera_A` / `vera_B` into the adapter file beside the per-layer
vectors.  `False` makes the file small and reloads the projections from
`projection_prng_key` (warns: it relies on the generator staying the same).

parameters.name: vera_dropout
parameters.description: Dropout on the update's input, in `[0, 1)`.

parameters.name: d_initial
parameters.description:
The value $\lambda_d$ starts at; small values (0.1 or less) are
recommended (Table 6c of the paper).

parameters.name: fan_in_fan_out
parameters.description:
For bases that store their weight `(in, out)`.  `nn.Linear` does not,
so `True` warns and is reset to `False`.

parameters.name: bias
parameters.description:
The reference also offers `"all"` and `"vera_only"`; here the adapter
trains its own vectors only, and those raise `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: modules_to_save
parameters.description: Modules trained in full beside the adapter (a classifier head).

parameters.name: init_weights
parameters.description:
`True`: $\lambda_d = d_{initial}$ and $\lambda_b = 0$.
`False`: $\lambda_d \sim \mathcal N(0, 1)$ and $\lambda_b = 1$
(the update is non-zero from the start — for tests).

parameters.name: layers_to_transform
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraConfig`.

parameters.name: layers_pattern
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraConfig`.

parameters.name: exclude_modules
parameters.description: Modules never adapted, matched like `target_modules`.

raises.description: A field holds a value of the wrong type.
A field is out of range or two fields conflict.
`bias` is not `"none"`.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.vera import VeraConfig
>>> config = VeraConfig(r=128, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"], projection_prng_key=7)
>>> sorted(config.target_modules), config.peft_type
(['q_proj', 'v_proj'], <PeftType.VERA: 'VERA'>)
>>> VeraConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True

members.name: Linear
members.signature: Linear(base_layer: nn.Module, adapter_name: str, config: VeraConfig, r: int = 0)
members.summary: An `nn.Linear` with a VeRA update: $y = W x + b + \lambda_b \odot B(\lambda_d \odot A\,\mathrm{drop}(x))$.

parameters.name: base_layer
parameters.description: The layer to adapt; kept as `base_layer`, its parameters shared.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in every table.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The adapter's config.

parameters.name: r
parameters.description: Rank; pass a positive one.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.vera import VeraConfig
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.vera import Linear
>>> base = nn.Linear(8, 4)
>>> layer = Linear(base, "default", VeraConfig(target_modules=["x"]), r=16)
>>> tuple(layer.vera_lambda_d["default"].shape), tuple(layer.vera_lambda_b["default"].shape)
((16,), (4,))
>>> x = lucid.randn(2, 8)
>>> bool((layer(x) == base(x)).all().item())   # lambda_b starts at zero
True

half-precision base.  A layer that holds an adapter already keeps applying
the adapters it applied: the new one is inactive until `set_adapter`
names it.  The projection the adapter reads is the layer's `bind`-ing.

methods.summary: Fold the update into the base weights, in place.
methods.extended:
The weights keep their identity — they are written, not replaced —
so whatever holds them (an optimizer, a tied embedding) sees the
merged values.  That is also why a weight shared with another
module must not be merged into; the tuner's `merge_adapter` and
`merge_and_unload` refuse it, as this layer alone cannot see the
rest of the model.

(`lora_bias` on a base with no bias).

members.summary: Adapter bookkeeping shared by the VeRA layers.
members.extended:
Holds the wrapped module as `base_layer` — the very module, so its
parameters stay the same `Parameter` objects — and, per adapter name, the
vectors of the adapter.  The forward pass adds the update of every active
adapter this layer holds; a layer given no projection (`bind`) draws one
from the key of its first adapter.

is stored `(out, in)`), or `base_layer` builds parameters on its first input.

applying the adapters it applied, and every parameter keeps the

methods.signature: merge_adapter(adapter_names: list[str] | None = None, safe_merge: bool = False)
methods.summary: Fold adapter updates into their base weights, keeping the adapter layers.
methods.extended:
A merged model runs at the base model's cost; `unmerge_adapter`
takes the updates out again.  Every refusal is made before any
weight is written: nothing is merged if a layer's base weight is
shared with another module (a tied LM head — merging would change
that module too) or if the adapter is disabled.

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Merge the adapters into the base weights and return the plain model.
methods.extended:
Each adapter layer is replaced by its merged base module — the base
model's own module, holding its own `Parameter` objects — and each
`modules_to_save` entry by the active adapter's trained copy (the
original when that adapter has none).  Adapters not merged are
dropped with their layers.  Every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

returns.description: The model, merged, with no adapter layer left in it.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or a
`modules_to_save` module shared one (its trained copy would
break the tie).

methods.name: unload
methods.summary: Remove every adapter without merging and return the original model.
methods.extended:
Every adapter layer is replaced by the module it wrapped (a merged
one is unmerged first), every `modules_to_save` entry by its
original module, and every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

members.summary: A model with VeRA layers put into it, the projections they share, and the tools to take them out.
members.extended:
Construction replaces each `nn.Linear` `config` selects with a VeRA
layer around it and freezes every other parameter.  The model is changed in
place and kept as `model`; a public name this wrapper lacks is read from
it.  `config` itself is not changed: `peft_config` holds a copy with the
default `target_modules` spelled out.

The two random projections $A$ and $B$ are drawn once, sized for
the largest targeted layer, and held here as `vera_A` / `vera_B`
(containers of one tensor per adapter, aliased when adapters share them) —
the reference's attributes.  Every layer reads them from there; the first
layer holds them in its module tree, so a state dict lists each once
(`<layer>.vera_A.<adapter>`) and the adapter file holds one pair.
Adapters added later must fit them (the same `projection_prng_key` and
`save_projection`, a rank and layer sizes no larger).

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to adapt.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in every `vera_lambda_*` table.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

parameters.name: state_dict
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

raises.description:
No module matches `target_modules`, a match is not an `nn.Linear`,
`modules_to_save` matches nothing, or an adapter does not fit the
projections of the first.

The model already holds adapter layers (wrap it once; add adapters
with `add_adapter`).

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.vera import VeraConfig, VeraModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(8, 2))
>>> vera = VeraModel(net, VeraConfig(r=4, target_modules=["0", "2"]), "default")
>>> tuple(vera.vera_A["default"].shape), tuple(vera.vera_B["default"].shape)
((4, 8), (8, 4))
>>> net[0].base_layer.weight.requires_grad, net[0].vera_lambda_d["default"].requires_grad
(False, True)
>>> vera.unload() is net, type(net[0]) is nn.Linear
(True, True)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.vera` — VeRA: two learned vectors per layer over shared random projections.
extended:
VeRA (Kopiczko et al., 2023, [arXiv:2310.11454](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11454) — Vector-based Random Matrix Adaptation) draws one
random pair $A$, $B$ once and shares it, frozen, across every adapted layer; a layer
learns only a vector $\lambda_d$ of length `r` and a vector $\lambda_b$ of its output
width, $y = Wx + \lambda_b\odot B(\lambda_d\odot Ax)$.  Far fewer parameters than LoRA at the
same rank, so ranks run much higher; the projections can be regenerated from `projection_prng_key`
(`save_projection=False`), so a file can hold only the vectors.  Pick it for the smallest
adapters, or many adapters on one base.

Where the reference library keeps them, so `isinstance(m, VeraLayer)` and `from
lucid.peft.tuners.vera import VeraConfig, Linear` read as they do there.  One layer type for the
one module the method adapts, `nn.Linear`.  `VeraConfig` and `VeraModel` (which holds the
shared projections) are here and exported from `lucid.peft`.  Importing the package registers the
method (its config under `PeftType.VERA`, its tuner and layer), which is what makes
`get_peft_model` and `PeftModel.from_pretrained` know it.
citation: Kopiczko, Dawid J., et al. "VeRA: Vector-based Random Matrix Adaptation." [arXiv:2310.11454](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11454), 2023.
theory:
VeRA (Kopiczko et al., 2023, [arXiv:2310.11454](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11454) — Vector-based Random Matrix
Adaptation) freezes the model **and** the low-rank pair: one random matrix
$A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{in}}$ and one
$B \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times r}$ are drawn once and shared by every
targeted layer (sliced to its size), and a layer learns only two vectors,

$$
\qquad \lambda_d \in \mathbb{R}^{r},\; \lambda_b \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}.
$$
